rawFindings.title: Regression: 'Allow' header for OPTIONS may contain duplicate methods
rawFindings.explanation: The change replaces a call to 'appendMethods', which ensured uniqueness of HTTP methods in the 'Allow' header, with a direct 'options.push.apply' call that blindly concatenates route methods. This introduces duplicate HTTP methods in the 'Allow' header response to OPTIONS requests, breaking expected behavior and potentially causing interoperability issues.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore uniqueness logic for HTTP methods in the 'Allow' header. Either revert line 210 to use 'appendMethods(options, route._options())', and keep the 'appendMethods' function, or re-implement unique insertion to 'options' array to avoid duplicates.

rawFindings.title: Regression: Duplicate HTTP methods in OPTIONS response Allow header
rawFindings.explanation: The change replaces a deduplicating appendMethods() call with a simple push.apply() to add HTTP methods to the OPTIONS response list, which allows duplicate methods to appear in the Allow header, breaking the previous behavior tested by test/app.options.js.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the deduplication logic by keeping or re-adding the appendMethods() function usage when adding route._options() to the options array.

rawFindings.title: Regression: Duplicate HTTP methods in 'Allow' header for OPTIONS requests
rawFindings.explanation: The change replaces the 'appendMethods' function call, which avoided adding duplicate methods, with a direct push of all methods from route._options(), risking duplicates in the 'options' array. This breaks deduplication for the 'Allow' header values sent on OPTIONS requests.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the deduplication behavior by using a function that adds only unique methods to 'options'. Reintroduce the appendMethods function or a similar deduplication mechanism, and replace the direct 'options.push.apply(...)' call with that function.
